citations.title: Title and Purpose (proposed CLA rules)
citations.requirement: Minimum operating requirements for CLAs serving up to four adults with a developmental disability who receive intense residential services authorized or financially supported by DBHDD. Services follow each resident's ISP and include daily personal services. RULE STATUS: DBHDD published the text as a proposed rule (Board draft 6/18/26; notice reissued 7/22/26). The DBHDD rules page still listed it under 'Proposed' when fetched on 10/14/2026. No adoption notice was found. Confirm with DBHDD Legal before relying on it.

citations.title: Exemptions (proposed)
citations.requirement: Chapter does not apply to personal care homes (Ch. 290-5-35 and other DCH-licensed facilities), DBHDD-funded host homes, crisis homes, DBHDD community integration homes, or community care homes. Host-home CRA sites are therefore outside CLA licensure under this draft. DBHDD's manuals still address them separately.

citations.title: Definitions (proposed)
citations.requirement: Defines CLA as a group home for up to four individuals with DD. Also defines Corrective Action Plan (problem statement, causes, steps, target dates, responsible persons by full name and title), employee and direct access, registry check, representative (guardian; spouse; adult child; parent; attorney; adult next of kin; adult friend), restraint, seclusion, medical support device, proxy caregiver, and the four medication pathways.

citations.title: Governing Body (proposed)
citations.requirement: Governing body is responsible for compliance with the O.C.G.A. and DBHDD rules. It names the administrator in the license application. No governing body member, staff or staff family may serve as a resident's representative or guardian. No one may solicit a resident to name staff as a beneficiary of a will, trust or life insurance. Gifts must be investigated, and involuntary gifts reported to law enforcement and the legal representative. No life insurance may be taken on a resident. Written policies must exist before a license is issued and must be followed.

citations.title: Required Policies and Procedures of the Governing Body (proposed)
citations.requirement: Minimum policy list: (a) code of conduct, signed annually; (b) scope of services; (c) no admission or retention of persons needing more care than can be provided; (d) rights; (e) medication management, including all four pathways; (f) abuse, neglect, exploitation, incident, injury, change-in-condition and death reporting; (g) medical support devices and restrictive interventions; (h) admissions, discharge, refunds and record transfer; (i) QA with an injury indicator; (j) staffing and training; (k) levels of observation; (l) resident conduct; (m) infection control; (n) confidentiality and a written emergency plan covering medical, weather, manmade, utility, fire and elopement (report within 30 minutes under Mattie's Call Act); (o) responsible staff person.

citations.title: Licenses (proposed)
citations.requirement: No CLA may operate or serve residents without a valid DBHDD license. Application requires a floor sketch, full ownership disclosure, records and criminal checks for owners and employees, and proof of electrical, water, sewage and fire safety compliance. License must be posted and is non-transferable. It is invalid on cessation, relocation, a change of more than 50% of ownership, or a significant change of the governing body. Notify DBHDD within 15 calendar days of any ownership change. One license per residence. Capacity may not exceed 4. A provisional license of up to 6 months is available only for a former PCH, and only with an acceptable CAP. NOTE: the draft text contains two numbered (1)-(8) series under .06.

citations.title: Investigations, Surveys and Corrective Action Plans (proposed)
citations.requirement: Surveys may be announced or unannounced. Records must be produced, and residents and staff must be available for interview. A written CAP is due within 15 days of the survey report. Violations may be disputed within 10 days if an acceptable CAP is also submitted. The survey report must be available for inspection at the residence on request by any person.

citations.title: Administration (proposed)
citations.requirement: Administrator at least 21 years old; all employees at least 18. No employee works alone with residents until all minimum training and documented competence are complete. Personnel file contents: eligible criminal background determination, MVR, TB screening on hire (risk assessment, symptom evaluation, test; repeat on known exposure), first aid and BCLS training and recertification, and training and competency evidence including 16 hours of continuing education annually. Employees must be free of illegal drugs and alcohol, and of legal substances that impair duties. Before employment, a registry check, records check application and criminal background check are required (O.C.G.A. 37-1-141, 37-1-143).

citations.title: Staffing (proposed)
citations.requirement: Enough qualified, trained staff on duty to protect health, safety and welfare, with a staffing ratio sufficient to evacuate all residents within three minutes. Staff may not use the home as a personal residence. Staff must be awake in the home at all times during their scheduled shift. If residents are present without staff, the ISP must document assessed capacity to be independent. Maintain a monthly coverage plan made in advance, a record of actual coverage, and a plan for required services. Residents are not staff and may not be required to do staff tasks unless the ISP documents voluntary participation.

citations.title: Physical Plant Health and Safety Standards (proposed)
citations.requirement: Bedrooms: at least 80 sq ft usable floor space per person (not counting a built-in closet), no more than 2 residents, at least one window, closable doors, no double-cylinder locks. Bathrooms: one toilet, lavatory and shower per 4 residents. Interior temperature 65-85F, with cooling when above 80F. Hot water at or below 120F. AC-powered interconnected smoke detectors with battery backup, audible with doors closed. Fire drills monthly, with at least 2 per year during sleeping hours, documented. 5-lb ABC extinguishers checked annually by a technician and monthly by staff. Exterior door locks must open without a key from inside. Evacuation plan, secondary exits, first-aid supplies and other standards in .10(1)-(27).

citations.title: Services (proposed)
citations.requirement: Room, meals and services must match resident needs, and an ISP is required for each resident. Three well-balanced meals 7 days a week, with the last meal no earlier than 5:00 PM and snacks offered mid-afternoon and evening. Special diets as prescribed. Food within its use-by date. Three-day non-perishable food supply and 1 gallon of water per person per day. Meal records kept 30 days. An individual file is kept for each resident, confidential, and available to the resident, guardian and Department.

citations.title: Admission (proposed)
citations.requirement: Do not admit or retain a resident whose needs exceed what the home can support. Administrator reviews records and interviews the individual. Physical exam within 12 months before admission, and TB screening within 12 months documented before admission. No services for persons not authorized or reimbursed by DBHDD. Written admission agreement signed by the CLA, resident and guardian, covering services, charges, 60 days' written notice of changes, refund policy, valuables and cooperative-living expectations. Resident may read the agreement or receive reasonable accommodation. Copies to the resident and guardian.

citations.title: Discharge or Transfer of a Resident (proposed)
citations.requirement: Admission agreement includes a written discharge and transfer procedure. 30 days' written notice with the reason to the resident and representative, with a copy to the DBHDD regional field office. Expedited transfer if the resident needs continuous medical or nursing care beyond the CLA's capability, or behavior directly and substantially threatens health or safety. Within 24 hours of discharge or transfer, provide a full file (digital or paper) to the receiving provider and document the reason, notifications and destination.

citations.title: Medications (proposed)
citations.requirement: Four pathways: proxy caregiver, assisted self-administration, self-directed self-administration, or licensed professional. Order or prescription signed within the past year for every medication. Initial orders procured within 24 hours; refills before the supply is exhausted. Only physicians or pharmacists may repackage or dispense. Medications are locked; refrigerated medications are kept at 36-41F. Training by a physician, physician extender, RN or pharmacist, with annual competency testing. Emergency medications (epinephrine, seizure rescue, glucagon, naloxone) may be given by non-licensed staff. A monthly MAR is required for every method of administration. Written policy elements are in .14(14).

citations.title: Rights of Residents (proposed)
citations.requirement: Right to complain to DBHDD and to report suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation or abandonment privately, even over a guardian's objection. No retaliation. Non-waivable rights include nondiscriminatory services, voting and choices, bedroom privacy (staff knock), private uncensored communication, freedom from mechanical or chemical restraint and seclusion, control of property, visitors at agreed times, telephone access, managing own money, personal needs allowance, choice of physician, participation in care planning, access to and copies of own records, and posting of DBHDD and regional field office phone numbers.

citations.title: Medical Support Devices (proposed)
citations.requirement: A device qualifies if prescribed or recommended by a physician or extender, used for a documented medical or therapeutic purpose, and the least restrictive option. Before first use: a physician's written order (type, rationale, duration, release and monitoring) filed in the record, discussion with the resident and guardian, and authorization in the ISP and PBSP or crisis/safety plan. Staff are trained. Devices are inspected before use and discontinued by physician order. NOTE: the draft body labels this section 'Rule 83-13-1-.16' while the TOC says 82-13-1-.16.

citations.title: Restraints (proposed)
citations.requirement: Never permitted: chemical restraint, seclusion, restraint devices that are not medical support devices, and prone restraint (even within a benchmarked program). Restraint is a last resort, specified in the ISP, PBSP or crisis/safety plan. Staff need current nationally benchmarked crisis-intervention training. Release when the danger ends. Check the resident at least every 15 minutes, and check pressure sites. Notify the representative or guardian by phone within 24 hours. Document the interventions tried and all checks. Report incidents that meet DBHDD criteria. Monitor use to minimize restraint.

citations.title: Change in Condition or Serious or Unusual Incident (proposed)
citations.requirement: Immediately obtain needed care and notify the emergency contact, representative or guardian. The administrator or designee reports to DBHDD in the form it accepts (DBHDD may require an online platform). Document a summary with follow-up and notifications. On a death, immediately notify next of kin, physician and representative or guardian, observe death-reporting statutes, and report to DBHDD.

citations.title: Reporting to the Department (proposed)
citations.requirement: Report all reportable incidents to DBHDD in the form and electronic system DBHDD specifies. DBHDD may open a separate investigation of an incident.

citations.title: Enforcement and Sanctions (proposed)
citations.requirement: DBHDD may refuse an initial license, revoke a license or impose sanctions under Ch. 82-14-1. Requirements may be suspended during a Governor-declared public health emergency.

citations.title: Variances and Waivers (proposed)
citations.requirement: DBHDD may grant variances and waivers on forms it provides, on a showing of undue hardship or equivalent protection, subject to conditions.

citations.cite: DBHDD Public Notice of Proposed Rules, Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 82-13-1 (rev. 7/22/2026)
citations.title: Public notice and economic impact statement
citations.requirement: Proposed rules replace 290-9-37 following HB 584 (2025). Comments were due 8/21/2026, 5:00 PM, to legal@dbhdd.ga.gov. Board consideration was set for 8/27/2026. DBHDD calls awake staff a 'longstanding expectation' tied to the Medicaid State Plan rate methodology (24-hour awake staff). The notice lists the four medication pathways, 24-hour file transfer, and 15-day CAP and 10-day dispute timelines. DBHDD Legal: 404.657.2282.

citations.title: Status of CLA rules
citations.requirement: Lists 82-14 Licensure Enforcement and Sanctions as adopted. Lists the CLA rules (82-13-1) only under 'Proposed New Rules & Regulations.' This is the basis for treating 82-13-1 as not yet effective.

citations.title: General Licensing Requirements and Fee Schedules (ADOPTED, eff. June 4, 2026)
citations.requirement: No facility may offer services requiring a license without a current DBHDD license. No license is issued unless the facility is substantially in compliance and fees are paid. An application is not acted on until complete with all attachments and fees. Annual fees are due on the anniversary of the prior license (30 days from invoice). DBHDD may revoke for annual fees unpaid 60 days after invoice. Fee schedule: $300 application processing (new, ownership change, name change, service-level change requiring a site visit); CLA annual $350; initial license fee 'same as annual' (but DBHDD's fee table lists $650; confirm); $150 late fee at 60 days; $250 follow-up visit; fees non-refundable; 25% discount if accredited by a DBHDD-approved body.

citations.title: Enforcement (ADOPTED)
citations.requirement: Sanctions may follow knowingly false statements or falsified records, refusal of access to the premises or information, or failure to comply with licensing requirements. Notice of intent to sanction is issued within 90 days of an application or of discovering the grounds.

citations.title: Sanctions (ADOPTED)
citations.requirement: Sanctions include public reprimand (posted 90 days), suspension, prohibiting persons in management or control, revocation, civil fines, and limiting or restricting a license. Fines up to $2,000 per violation per day, capped at $40,000 per survey. Categories: Critical $1,201-$2,000; High $601-$1,200; Moderate $300-$600; Low no fine. Suspension and revocation notices must be posted. The Commissioner may issue emergency orders for CLAs in imminent and substantial danger: relocation, a monitor for up to 10 days, and prohibition or suspension of admissions.

citations.title: Surveys, Investigations and Corrective Action Plans (ADOPTED)
citations.requirement: Surveys and investigations may be announced or unannounced. A license application or license is consent to entry. Staff must cooperate and produce documents without unreasonable delay. A CAP is due within 15 days of a written report of violations, with at least one opportunity to revise an unacceptable CAP, and the facility must comply with the accepted CAP. DBHDD may require an internal CAP. A facility may explain or dispute findings within 10 days, following the instructions DBHDD includes with the report.

citations.title: Applicability of Administrative Procedures Act (ADOPTED)
citations.requirement: A hearing request on any sanction must be in writing and submitted to DBHDD no later than 10 calendar days after receipt of the notice of intent to sanction.

citations.title: Purpose; Applicability (current codified CLA rules)
citations.requirement: Minimum operating requirements for CLAs serving two or more adults whose residential services are financially supported by DBHDD-designated funds (text still refers to DHR/DMHDDAD). These codified rules remain on the SOS site until replaced by 82-13-1.

citations.title: Governing Body (current codified)
citations.requirement: Governing body is responsible for compliance and names the administrator in its application. No governing body member, staff or staff family may serve as a resident's representative or guardian. No inducement to name staff as beneficiary. Gifts investigated. No life insurance on residents.

citations.title: Administration (current codified; policies before licensure)
citations.requirement: Each residence develops written policies before a license is issued and follows them. Required contents include a service description, no admission or retention beyond capability, guarantee of rights, medication supervision, procedures for reporting and investigating abuse, neglect, exploitation, incidents, accidents, injuries, changes in condition and death, admissions, discharge and immediate transfer, refunds, cooperative living, and QA with an injury indicator. The fetched text was truncated after .07(3)(j); remaining legacy sections were not retrieved.

citations.title: Licenses (legacy text, as provided in research)
citations.requirement: Governing body must hold a valid license or provisional license before beginning operation. The research flags current status as not verified, and the text was not re-fetched in this pass.

citations.cite: DBHDD Provider Manual for Community DD Providers (FY27 Q2, eff. 10/1/2026), Part II, Sec. 1, Organizational Practices, A
citations.title: Program Structure
citations.requirement: Written service description, policies and org chart. Code of conduct signed annually by all employees and contractors. Program description states minimum staff-to-individual ratios and defines 1:1 arm's-length and line-of-sight staffing. Residential licenses are required where applicable. General liability insurance naming DBHDD as certificate holder at $1 million per occurrence and $3 million aggregate. Full access for DBHDD and state and federal reviewers. Provider must earn and keep an ASO Quality Review score of 85% or higher and comply with Policy 02-703. Written budget. Written statement on whether research is conducted. Supervisory sign-off of service notes and timesheets.

citations.cite: DBHDD DD Provider Manual (FY27 Q2), Part II, Sec. 1, Organizational Practices, B
citations.title: Oversight of Contracted Providers/Professionals
citations.requirement: Provider holds the CLA License (or PCH Permit for pre-July-2011 providers) for every CRA residential site. HFR-issued permits remain valid until DBHDD issues a new license. CRA subcontracting is restricted to Host Home Providers. All nursing under a CLA license needs site-specific nursing enrollment and must meet the NOW/COMP Part II and III contracting requirements. Quarterly report to the Board on contracted providers, and a report to the Regional Field Office before the end of FY Q1 and Q3.

citations.cite: DBHDD DD Provider Manual (FY27 Q2), Part II, Sec. 1, Organizational Practices, C
citations.title: Quality Improvement and Risk Management
citations.requirement: Written QI plan reviewed at least annually. Monitored risk areas include incidents, complaints, rights violations, restrictive interventions (reviewed by the organization's Rights Sub-Committee), medication management, infection control, confidentiality breaches, ISP implementation and community integration. Quarterly indicator review and distribution of findings. At least 4 records or 5% of individuals (whichever is greater) reviewed each quarter, kept 2 years. Advisory board meets at least semi-annually.

citations.cite: DBHDD DD Provider Manual (FY27 Q2), Part II, Sec. 1, Medication and Healthcare Management (CRITICAL), D
citations.title: Medication and Healthcare Management
citations.requirement: Physician order or prescription signed within the past year on file for every medication. Psychotropic informed consent and capacity process using O.C.G.A. 31-9-2 priority order. Written medication policies on prescribing, procuring within 24 hours, labeling, locked storage, refrigeration at 36-41F with daily logs, double-locked controlled substances, dispensing by pharmacist or physician only, and supervision of self-administration. Only licensed persons administer. Proxy caregiver rules, polypharmacy review, AIMS every 12 months where indicated, and prescriber notification of errors. Biennial independent pharmacist or RN medication-management assessment at every site housing medications. Individualized healthcare plans (Policies 02-266, 02-807). Eight rights; MAR content and legend.

citations.cite: DBHDD DD Provider Manual (FY27 Q2), Part II, Sec. 1, Adequate and Competent Staff (CRITICAL), E
citations.title: Adequate and Competent Staff
citations.requirement: At least one DDP. In 24-hour residential settings, at least one staff trained in BCLS/BLS and first aid on duty every shift. Verify licenses and credentials. FLSA compliance. Job descriptions. Criminal records checks per Policy 04-104, MVR checks, and TB testing before hire and on known exposure. For CLAs, a five-year employment history verified by the administrator. Orientation before direct contact (HIPAA, rights, mandatory ABE reporting, HCBS Settings Rule). Within 60 days, non-designated staff complete the full training list. Minimum 16 hours of training annually. Annual competency validation and performance evaluation.

citations.cite: DBHDD DD Provider Manual (FY27 Q2), Part II, Sec. 1, Outcomes for Persons Served, A (Individual Rights)

policies.category: Code of conduct, including prohibited acts, employee reporting process, annual signed acknowledgment and discipline
policies.title: Code of Conduct and Prohibited Acts
state_specifics: The code addresses appropriate use of resources, conflicts of interest and due professional care.
Never permitted: abandonment, threats (overt or implied), corporal punishment, fear-eliciting procedures, abuse or neglect.
Never permitted: withholding nutrition or nutritional care, or basic necessities (clothing, shelter, rest or sleep).
No staff may solicit residents to name staff as will, trust or life-insurance beneficiaries.
Gifts from residents are investigated. Involuntary gifts go to law enforcement and the legal representative.

policies.category: Code of conduct, including prohibited acts, employee reporting process, annual signed acknowledgment and discipline
policies.title: Employee Reporting of Unacceptable Behavior, Annual Acknowledgment and Discipline
state_specifics: Written process tells employees what to do when they learn of unacceptable behavior.
All employees and contractors sign the code at least annually (also a DBHDD provider manual requirement).
Appropriate disciplinary action follows departures from policy or violations of the code.
Signed acknowledgments are kept in the personnel file.

policies.title: Scope of Services and Population Served
state_specifics: Proposed 82-13-1 serves up to 4 adults with a developmental disability. Current codified 290-9-37 applies to 2 or more adults.
Services are DBHDD-authorized or financially supported (CRA through state funds and NOW/COMP) and follow each resident's ISP.
Services include daily personal services. Room, meals and services must match resident needs.
The description states the population served, the services available and how residents' needs and desires are addressed.
No services to persons not authorized or reimbursed by DBHDD.

policies.title: Admission Eligibility and Limits on Retention
state_specifics: Do not admit or retain a resident whose needs exceed what the home can support.
The administrator reviews records and interviews the individual before admission.
Physical exam within 12 months and TB screening within 12 months before admission, documented.
Staffing capacity, including the 3-minute evacuation standard, is checked against the resident's mobility and ISP.
Admissions come through a DBHDD Regional Field Office referral.

policies.title: Resident Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: Non-waivable rights include nondiscriminatory services, voting and choices, and bedroom privacy (staff knock).
Non-waivable rights also include private uncensored communication, telephone access and visitors at agreed times.
Residents are free from mechanical or chemical restraint and seclusion.
Residents keep control of their property, manage their own money and have a personal needs allowance.
Residents may choose their physician, take part in care planning and get copies of their records.
Post DBHDD and regional field office phone numbers. Rights training happens at orientation.

policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Non-Retaliation
state_specifics: Residents may complain to DBHDD at any time.
Residents may report suspected abuse, neglect, exploitation or abandonment privately, even over a guardian's objection.
No retaliation against a resident or staff member who complains or reports.
Complaints and rights violations are tracked as QI risk areas and reviewed quarterly.
Post DBHDD and regional field office phone numbers where residents can see them.

policies.title: Personal Funds, Property and Personal Needs Allowance
state_specifics: Residents control their property and manage their own money. They receive a personal needs allowance.
Keep resident money separate from agency funds, with a ledger and receipts.
Valuables handling and any charges are stated in the signed admission agreement. Changes need 60 days' written notice.
Get written DBHDD and SSA guidance on how the CRA per diem interacts with SSI before charging residents.
No life insurance may be taken on a resident.

policies.title: Informed Consent, Representatives and Decision-Making Support
state_specifics: The representative may be a guardian, spouse, adult child, parent, attorney, adult next of kin or adult friend.
No governing body member, staff member or staff family member may serve as a resident's representative or guardian.
Psychotropic medication informed consent and capacity process follows the O.C.G.A. 31-9-2 priority order.
Residents take part in care planning and may read the admission agreement or receive reasonable accommodation.
Restraints and medical support devices need the resident's and guardian's discussion and ISP authorization.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d)
state_specifics: Nondiscriminatory services are a non-waivable resident right.
Reasonable accommodation so residents can read or understand the admission agreement.
Provide interpreters or accessible formats at admission, rights review and ISP meetings.
Copies of agreements go to the resident and guardian.

policies.title: Medication Management and Supervision
state_specifics: Four pathways (proposed .14): proxy caregiver, assisted self-administration, self-directed self-administration, licensed professional.
Every medication needs an order or prescription signed within the past year. Initial orders are procured within 24 hours, and refills before supply runs out.
A monthly MAR is required for every method of administration.
Only physicians or pharmacists may repackage or dispense.
The policy covers orders, procurement, storage, security, administration, documentation and disposal.

policies.title: Determining Administration Method and Self-Administration Capacity
state_specifics: Assess each resident's capacity to self-administer before choosing a pathway, and record the result in the ISP.
Written actions to take when concerns about self-administration capacity arise.
Polypharmacy review and AIMS every 12 months where indicated.
Biennial independent pharmacist or RN medication-management assessment at every site housing medications.

policies.title: Medication Emergencies, Errors and Allergy Flagging
state_specifics: Emergency procedure lists who to notify, the local poison information center number, the decision-maker and the physician, clinic or ER to contact.
Define medication errors, document and report them, and notify the prescriber.
Non-licensed staff may give emergency medications: epinephrine, seizure rescue, glucagon, naloxone.
Flag allergies and other critical information on the MAR and in the record.

policies.title: Medication Storage, Disposal and Staff Medication Training
state_specifics: Medications are locked. Refrigerated medications are kept at 36-41F with daily logs.
Controlled substances are double-locked.
Disposal procedure for discontinued or out-of-date medications.
Training is delivered by a physician, physician extender, RN or pharmacist, with annual competency testing.
Only trained staff administer or assist.

policies.category: Abuse, neglect, exploitation and incident reporting
policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Orientation before direct contact covers mandatory ABE reporting.
Residents may report privately, and no one may retaliate.
Report to DBHDD in the form and electronic system it specifies. Confirm current ABE timelines in the DBHDD provider manual.
Notify the RSA-DD within 2 hours of any death or high-visibility incident.
DBHDD may open a separate investigation.

policies.category: Abuse, neglect, exploitation and incident reporting
policies.title: Reportable Incidents, Accidents, Injuries and Investigations
state_specifics: Immediately obtain needed care and notify the emergency contact, representative or guardian.
The administrator or designee reports to DBHDD in the form it accepts (DBHDD may require an online platform).
Document a summary with follow-up and notifications.
Any injury to a resident is a required QA indicator.
Incidents are reviewed at least weekly and quarterly for trends.

policies.category: Abuse, neglect, exploitation and incident reporting
policies.title: Death of a Resident
state_specifics: On a death, immediately notify next of kin, physician and representative or guardian.
Observe the death-reporting statutes.
Report to DBHDD, and notify the RSA-DD within 2 hours.
Refunds and transfer of belongings, funds and burial accounts follow the discharge policies.
Include the death in mortality review.

policies.category: Medical support devices and restrictive interventions
policies.title: Medical Support Devices and Restrictive Interventions
state_specifics: A device qualifies if a physician or extender prescribes or recommends it, it serves a documented medical or therapeutic purpose, and it is the least restrictive option.
Before first use: written order (type, rationale, duration, release, monitoring), resident and guardian discussion, and ISP and PBSP or crisis/safety plan authorization.
Never permitted: chemical restraint, seclusion, restraint devices that are not medical support devices, and prone restraint.
The Rights Sub-Committee reviews restrictive interventions.
The policy lists the devices and interventions the organization implements or prohibits.

policies.category: Medical support devices and restrictive interventions
policies.title: Minimizing Restraint and Positive Behavior Support
state_specifics: Restraint is a last resort, specified in the ISP, PBSP or crisis/safety plan. Staff need current nationally benchmarked crisis-intervention training.
Release when the danger ends. Check the resident at least every 15 minutes, including pressure sites.
Notify the representative or guardian by phone within 24 hours.
Document interventions tried and all checks. Report incidents meeting DBHDD criteria.
Monitor use of restraint to minimize it.

policies.category: Admissions and discharges, refunds, transfer of records and belongings, and cooperative living
policies.title: Admission Process and Admission Agreement
state_specifics: Written admission agreement signed by the CLA, resident and guardian.
The agreement covers services, charges, 60 days' written notice of changes, refund policy, valuables and cooperative-living expectations.
It includes the written discharge and transfer procedure.
Copies go to the resident and guardian.
Admit only persons authorized or reimbursed by DBHDD.

policies.category: Admissions and discharges, refunds, transfer of records and belongings, and cooperative living
policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Immediate Transfer
state_specifics: 30 days' written notice with the reason to the resident and representative, with a copy to the DBHDD regional field office.
Expedited transfer if the resident needs continuous medical or nursing care beyond the CLA's capability.
Expedited transfer if behavior directly and substantially threatens health or safety.
Within 24 hours, give the receiving provider a full file.
Document the reason, notifications and destination.

policies.category: Admissions and discharges, refunds, transfer of records and belongings, and cooperative living
policies.title: Refunds on Transfer, Discharge or Death
state_specifics: The refund policy is stated in the admission agreement.
It applies when a resident is transferred, discharged or dies.
Prepare a written calculation and return funds to the resident or representative or estate.
The researched rule text sets no refund deadline, so set one in the policy.
Resident funds are accounted for separately.

policies.category: Admissions and discharges, refunds, transfer of records and belongings, and cooperative living
policies.title: Transfer of Records, Medications, Belongings, Funds and Burial Accounts
state_specifics: Within 24 hours of discharge or transfer, provide the complete file (digital or paper) to the receiving provider.
Transfer unused special medical supplies, personal belongings, medications, funds and burial accounts.
Use a signed inventory and handoff.
Document the reason, notifications and destination.

policies.category: Admissions and discharges, refunds, transfer of records and belongings, and cooperative living
policies.title: Cooperative Living Expectations
state_specifics: Expectations are stated in the admission agreement.
Cooperative-living expectations may not override resident rights (privacy, visitors, personal property).
Residents are not staff and may not be required to do staff tasks unless the ISP documents voluntary participation.
Roommate limits: no more than 2 residents per bedroom.

policies.title: Internal Quality Assurance Program and Injury Indicator
state_specifics: Resident injury must be an indicator that is measured and improved.
Written QI plan reviewed at least annually.

Monitored risk areas include incidents, complaints, rights violations, restrictive interventions, medication management, infection control, confidentiality breaches, ISP implementation and community integration.
Quarterly indicator review and distribution of findings.
Review at least 4 records or 5% of individuals each quarter, whichever is greater. Keep the reviews 2 years.

policies.title: Quality Reporting, Mortality Review and Advisory Oversight
state_specifics: Quarterly QM reports are due Oct 16, Jan 17, Apr 17 and Jul 17 (FY27).
Advisory board meets at least semi-annually.
The provider must earn and keep an ASO Quality Review score of 85% or higher.
Mortality and incident data feed the QI plan.
Quarterly report to the Board on contracted providers.

policies.category: Staffing, staff training and credential verification
policies.title: Staffing Requirements, Coverage Plans and Awake Staff
state_specifics: Staff must be awake in the home at all times during their scheduled shift.
Staffing ratio must be enough to evacuate all residents within three minutes. The proposed rule sets no numeric ratio.
Maintain a monthly coverage plan made in advance, a record of actual coverage, and a plan for required services.
Staff may not use the home as a personal residence.
If residents are present without staff, the ISP must document their assessed capacity to be independent.

policies.category: Staffing, staff training and credential verification
policies.title: Professional Oversight and Assignment of Duties
state_specifics: Appropriate professional staff oversee services, review clinical documentation, and conduct assessments.
At least one DDP.
All nursing under a CLA license needs site-specific nursing enrollment.
Duties match position, training and experience, and the rights requirements. Residents are not used as staff.
Written job descriptions and supervisory sign-off of service notes and timesheets.

policies.category: Staffing, staff training and credential verification
policies.title: Credential Verification, Registry and Background Checks
state_specifics: Before employment, including a potential administrator: registry check, records check application and criminal background check (O.C.G.A. 37-1-141, 37-1-143).
Verify licenses, credentials, experience and competence.
The administrator verifies a five-year employment history for CLA staff.
Motor vehicle record check, and a criminal records check per DBHDD Policy 04-104.
Administrator at least 21 and all employees at least 18.

policies.category: Staffing, staff training and credential verification
policies.title: Orientation, Training and Competency
state_specifics: No employee works alone with residents until all minimum training and documented competence are complete.
Orientation before direct contact: HIPAA, rights, mandatory ABE reporting, HCBS Settings Rule.
Non-designated staff complete the full training list within 60 days.
16 hours of continuing education annually, with annual competency validation and performance evaluation.
First aid and BCLS training and recertification. At least one staff member trained in BCLS and first aid is on duty every shift.

policies.category: Staffing, staff training and credential verification
policies.title: Employee Health, TB Screening and Fitness for Duty
state_specifics: TB screening on hire (risk assessment, symptom evaluation, test). Repeat on known exposure.
Employees must be free of illegal drugs and alcohol, and of legal substances that impair duties.
Offer bloodborne pathogen training and hepatitis B vaccination per OSHA.
Screening records go in the personnel file.

policies.category: Staffing, staff training and credential verification
policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: File contents: eligible criminal background determination, MVR, TB screening, and first aid and BCLS evidence.
File contents also include training and competency evidence and 16 hours of annual continuing education.
Signed code of conduct acknowledgment.
Job description and performance evaluation.
Keep files at the home or readily available for unannounced surveys.

policies.category: Staffing, staff training and credential verification
policies.title: Staff Conduct Inconsistent with Policy and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Written process for handling acts by staff that conflict with agency policy.
No member of the governing body, staff or staff family may be a resident's representative or guardian.
Gifts are investigated. Involuntary gifts go to law enforcement and the legal representative.
Corrective or disciplinary action is documented in the personnel file.

policies.title: Levels of Observation and Supervision
state_specifics: Match observation level to each resident's clinical care and safety needs.
Define 1:1 arm's-length and line-of-sight staffing.
State minimum staff-to-individual ratios in the program description.
Document an independence assessment in the ISP before any resident is left without staff.

policies.title: Resident Conduct Inconsistent with Home Policy
state_specifics: Respond through positive behavior support, not punishment.
Never use chemical restraint, seclusion or prone restraint.
Do not infringe non-waivable resident rights as a consequence.
Involuntary discharge follows the 30-day notice process, with expedited transfer only for the conditions in the discharge policy.

policies.title: Infection and Infestation Control
state_specifics: Procedures for controlling and preventing infections and infestations in the residence.
Staff TB screening on hire and on known exposure.
Infection control is a monitored QI risk area.
Bloodborne pathogen exposure control plan and personal protective equipment.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and Secure Information Management
state_specifics: Secure, organized and confidential management of information, including electronic records.
The individual file is confidential and available to the resident, guardian and DBHDD.
Residents may access and get copies of their own records.
Confidentiality breaches are tracked as a QI risk area.
HIPAA is covered at staff orientation.

policies.title: Written Emergency Plan
state_specifics: Plan covers medical emergencies, weather and natural disasters, manmade disasters, utility interruptions, and fire, explosion or physical damage.
It also covers elopement, with its own policy EMG-02.
Keep a 3-day non-perishable food supply and 1 gallon of water per person per day.
Staffing must allow evacuation of all residents within 3 minutes.
Train staff on the plan and review it annually.

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement (Mattie's Call)
state_specifics: Report a missing resident to local law enforcement within 30 minutes of staff receiving actual knowledge (Mattie's Call Act).
Then notify the representative or guardian and report the incident to DBHDD.
Post the local law-enforcement number. Run a tabletop drill.
Record the time staff learned of it and the time of the police report.

policies.title: Fire Safety, Evacuation Plan and Drills
state_specifics: Evacuation plan with clear instructions is available in each residence, with secondary exits.
Drills monthly at alternating times and shifts, with at least 2 per year during sleeping hours, documented.
AC-powered interconnected smoke detectors with battery backup, audible with doors closed.
5-lb ABC extinguishers: annual technician check and monthly staff check.
Exterior door locks open without a key from inside.

policies.title: Designation of the Responsible Staff Person
state_specifics: The administrator designates a qualified staff member to act in the administrator's absence.
Residents may not serve as the responsible staff person.
Post or record the designation for each shift. The administrator must be at least 21.

policies.title: Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities; Adoption of Policies
state_specifics: Written policies must exist before a license is issued and must be followed.
The governing body is responsible for compliance and names the administrator in the license application.
No governing body member, staff member or staff family member may serve as a resident's representative or guardian.
Policies cover every item in proposed .05(8) and codified 290-9-37-.07(3).
A responsible staff person is designated.

policies.title: Licensure, Surveys, Corrective Action Plans and Sanctions
state_specifics: No operation without a valid DBHDD license. Post the license. It is non-transferable, with one license per residence and capacity of no more than 4.
Notify DBHDD within 15 calendar days of any ownership change.
CAP due within 15 days of the survey report. Disputes within 10 days with an acceptable CAP. Hearing requests within 10 calendar days of a notice of intent to sanction.
Fines up to $2,000 per violation per day, capped at $40,000 per survey.
Fees: $300 application, $350 annual, $150 late at 60 days, $250 follow-up visit. Confirm the initial fee ($650 per fee table) and due dates with DBHDD.

policies.title: Medicaid Compliance, Billing and Service Documentation
state_specifics: An executed, signed DBHDD contract is required before reimbursement.
Bill through Carelon Provider Connects against each person's approved ISP.
Monthly MIER due by the 10th for individuals without a prior authorization in IDDC.
CRA may be subcontracted only to Host Home Providers.
Confirm with DBHDD whether EVV applies to CRA per diem services.

policies.title: Policy Review, Document Control, Insurance and Rule Monitoring
state_specifics: Proposed 82-13-1 would replace 290-9-37 but was not verified as adopted. Confirm with DBHDD Legal (404.657.2282, legal@dbhdd.ga.gov).
Review policies at least annually and when each quarterly provider manual or final rule changes.
Version-control every policy and keep retired versions.
General liability insurance with DBHDD as certificate holder at $1 million per occurrence and $3 million aggregate.
Full access for DBHDD and state and federal reviewers.

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning, the ISP and Daily Documentation
state_specifics: An ISP is required for each resident, and services follow it.
The provider completes the HRST at least 90 days before each annual ISP, and the provider's nurse reviews and signs it.
Daily service notes are supervisor-signed.
The ISP authorizes any restrictive intervention or device.

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
state_specifics: Community integration is a monitored QI risk area.
Residents choose visitors, telephone access, and daily routines.
HCBS Settings Rule is covered at orientation.
Residents may not be required to do staff tasks unless the ISP documents voluntary participation.

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
state_specifics: All nursing under a CLA license needs site-specific nursing enrollment.
Individualized healthcare plans per DBHDD Policies 02-266 and 02-807.
HRST at least 90 days before each annual ISP, nurse-approved by signature.
Resident chooses their own physician.

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures and Choking Risk
state_specifics: Seizure rescue medications may be given by non-licensed staff.
Individualized healthcare plans address seizure and choking risk.
Staff are trained on each resident's plan before working alone.
Physician orders for any special diet or device.

policies.title: Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
state_specifics: Immediately obtain needed care and notify the emergency contact, representative or guardian.
The administrator or designee reports to DBHDD.
Document a summary with follow-up and notifications.
Death notifications follow the death policy.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
state_specifics: Three well-balanced meals 7 days a week, with the last meal no earlier than 5:00 PM.
Snacks offered mid-afternoon and evening.
Special diets as prescribed. Food within its use-by date.
3-day non-perishable supply and 1 gallon of water per person per day.
Keep meal records 30 days.

policies.title: Residential Environment and Physical Plant Standards
state_specifics: Bedrooms: at least 80 sq ft usable per person, no more than 2 residents, a window, closable doors, no double-cylinder locks.
Bathrooms: one toilet, lavatory and shower per 4 residents.
Interior temperature 65-85F, with cooling when above 80F.
Hot water at or below 120F.
First-aid supplies and the other standards in .10(1)-(27).

policies.title: Transportation and Vehicle Safety
state_specifics: Motor vehicle record check for staff who drive.
Drivers hold a valid license.
Business auto liability covers owned, non-owned and hired vehicles. Confirm limits with DBHDD.
Vehicle incidents are reported as incidents.

policies.title: Individual Records and Retention
state_specifics: An individual file is kept for each resident, confidential and available to the resident, guardian and DBHDD.
Meal records are kept 30 days. QA record reviews are kept 2 years.
A complete file transfers within 24 hours of discharge.
Confirm the retention period for resident records with the DBHDD contract or provider manual.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Report all reportable incidents to DBHDD in the form and electronic system it specifies.
Notify the RSA-DD within 2 hours of any death or high-visibility incident.
Monthly MIER by the 10th for individuals without a prior authorization in IDDC.
Quarterly QM reports due Oct 16, Jan 17, Apr 17 and Jul 17.
Report on contracted providers to the Regional Field Office before the end of FY Q1 and Q3.

documents.title: Rules and Regulations for Community Living Arrangements, Rule 290-9-37-.07 'Administration, Criminal History Background Checks' (current codified rule; subsections (1), (3) and (6))

documents.version: Current codified text as retrieved from rules.sos.ga.gov. It is the rule the DBHDD CLA Application Packet (v. 1/1/2026) points applicants to.
documents.how_used: Rule currently in force. Subsection (1) requires written policies and procedures before a license is issued. Subsection (3) lists what they must include. Subsection (6) requires a written emergency plan.

documents.title: [PROPOSED] Chapter 82-13-1 Community Living Arrangements, Rule 82-13-1-.05 'Governing Body', subsections (6), (7) and (8) 'Required Policies and Procedures', plus the cross-referenced policy requirements in .09, .10, .13, .14 and .17

documents.title: Community Living Arrangement Application Packet
documents.form_number: DBHDD Licensure Application, Version 1/1/2026 (no form number)
documents.issuer: Georgia DBHDD, Healthcare Facility Regulation / Licensure
documents.how_used: Checked for policy requirements and found none. The 11 initial-application items are all application paperwork: Secretary of State evidence, affidavit, ID, property proof, fire marshal report, electrical form, water/septic, floor plan, certificate of occupancy, and owner background check or attestation. It is cited only for submission mechanics (online GAHLES portal, 30-business-day initial review, questions to Licensure.Application@dbhdd.ga.gov).

required_items.text: Prior to being issued a license, each residence shall develop written policies and procedures outlining the responsibilities of the governing body of the Community Living Arrangement and of the residents that ensure compliance with these rules.
A description of the services the residence intends to provide;
How the residence ensures that it does not admit or retain persons who require more care than the residence can provide;
How the residence guarantees the rights of residents;
How the residence supervises medications;
Procedures for reporting and investigating abuse, neglect, exploitation, incidents, accidents, injuries, and changes in a resident's condition, including death;
How the residence handles admissions;
Procedures for discharge and immediate transfers;
How refunds are handled when a resident is transferred, is discharged, or dies;
Expectations regarding cooperative living;

The quality assurance procedures that shall be used to maintain or improve the quality of care and services provided to the residents, including indicators of performance that shall be routinely measured and evaluated. At a minimum, the residence shall include as an indicator to be measured and improved, as necessary, any injury to a resident;
How the residence will ensure that staff are trained; and
How the residence handles acts committed by staff or residents that are inconsistent with policies of the residence.
Each residence shall have a written plan that effectively addresses the Community Living Arrangement's strategy for responding to the following emergency situations:
Local and widespread weather emergencies or natural disasters, such as tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes, ice or snow storms, or floods;
Manmade disasters such as acts of terrorism and hazardous materials spills;
Unanticipated interruption of service of utilities, including water, gas, or electricity, either within the facility or within a local or widespread area;
Fire, explosion, or other physical damage to the residence; and

Reporting the elopement of any disabled person from a Community Living Arrangement to local law enforcement within 30 minutes of the Community Living Arrangement staff receiving actual knowledge that such person is missing.

Prior to being issued a license, each residence shall develop written policies and procedures outlining the responsibilities of the governing body of the Community Living Arrangement that ensure compliance with these rules.
Required Policies and Procedures. The policies and procedures of the governing body shall include, but may not be limited to, the following:
A formal code of conduct communicating appropriate ethical and moral behavioral standards.
The code of conduct directly addresses issues such as appropriate use of resources, conflicts of interest, and use of due professional care.

The code of conduct makes it clear that under no circumstances will the following occur: (i) Abandonment of a resident; (ii) Threats (overt or implied) of harm or mistreatment of a resident; (iii) Corporal punishment of a resident; (iv) Fear-eliciting procedures directed toward a resident; (v) Any kind of abuse or neglect of a resident; (vi) Withholding basic nutrition or nutritional care from a resident; or (vii) Withholding from a resident any basic necessity such as clothing, shelter, rest or sleep.
The code of conduct provides a process for what employees must do if they become aware of unacceptable behavior.
The code of conduct is acknowledged by signature of all employees and contractors at least annually.
Appropriate disciplinary action is taken in response to departures from approved policies or violations of the code of conduct.

A description of the scope of services the residence intends to provide to include the population served, the services available, and how the organization plans to address the needs and desires of those served;
How the residence ensures that it does not admit or retain persons who require more care than the residence can provide, as outlined in Section .12 of these Rules.
How the residence guarantees the rights of the residents as outlined in Section .15 of these Rules.

Procedures for all aspects of medication management including but not limited to medication orders and procurement, storage, security, method(s) of administration used (proxy caregiver, licensed healthcare professional, assistance with self-administration or self-directed self-administration), documentation of all aspects of medication management, and disposal of discontinued or out of date medications as outlined in Section .14 of these Rules.
Procedures for reporting abuse, neglect, exploitation, incidents, accidents, injuries, and changes in a resident's condition, including death;

Procedures that outline and identify the medical support devices and other restrictive interventions that are implemented or prohibited by the organization and licensure requirements as outlined in Sections .16 and .17 of these Rules.
How the residence handles admissions and discharges, including:
Procedures for discharge/transfer/immediate transfer due to medical or behavioral needs of residents;
How refunds are handled when a resident is transferred, is discharged, or dies;
How the resident's complete record, unused special medical supplies, personal belongings, medications, funds and burial accounts are transferred when a resident is transferred or discharged.
Expectations regarding cooperative living.

The internal quality assurance procedures that shall be used to minimize risk and maintain or improve the quality of care and services provided to the residents, including processes for how deficiencies and risks are identified and managed on an ongoing basis. At a minimum, the residence shall include as an indicator to be measured and improved, as necessary, any injury to a resident;
What constitutes the staffing requirements and how the residence will ensure that staff are trained, including but not limited to the following required elements:

Policy demonstrates that appropriate professional staff oversee the services, support, care and treatment provided including reviewing clinical documentation, conducting assessments, developing behavior support plans, service plans, healthcare plans, and other protocols, and implementing assessment, care and treatment activities as defined in professional practice acts.
Procedures for verifying licenses, credentials, experience and competence of staff.
Personnel shall be assigned duties consistent with their position, training, and experience and with the requirements of Section .15 of these rules.
How the residence handles acts committed by staff that are inconsistent with policies of the residence.
Levels of observation procedures to meet the residents' clinical care and safety needs;
How the residence handles acts committed by residents that are inconsistent with the policies of the residence.
Procedures for controlling and preventing infections and infestations in the residence.

Procedures that support secure, organized and confidential management of information, including electronic records if applicable, that addresses state and federal confidentiality laws and regulations.
required_items.cite: 82-13-1-.05(8)(n) (proposed; the draft labels two consecutive items '(n)')

required_items.text: Each residence shall have a written plan that effectively addresses the Community Living Arrangement's strategy for responding to the following emergency situations: 1. Medical emergencies; 2. Local and widespread weather emergencies or natural disasters, such as tornadoes, hurricanes, earthquakes, ice or snow storms, or floods; 3. Manmade disasters such as acts of terrorism and hazardous materials spills; 4. Unanticipated interruption of service utilities, including water, gas, or electricity, within the facility or within a local or widespread area; 5. Fire, explosion, or other physical damage to the residence; and 6. Reporting the elopement (Georgia's Mattie's Call Act) of any disabled person from a Community Living Arrangement to local law enforcement within 30 minutes of the Community Living Arrangement staff receiving actual knowledge that such person is missing.

The Community Living Arrangement administrator shall designate a qualified staff member as the responsible staff person to act on his or her behalf and to carry out his or her duties in the administrator's absence. Residents of the Community Living Arrangement may not serve as the responsible staff person.
Community Living Arrangements shall have a written policy that specifies the procedures to be followed regarding oversight of medication. Such policy shall include but may not be limited to:

Processes for determining the method(s) of medication administration that may be used for residents, including an assessment to determine the resident's capacity to self-administer medications, as applicable.
Actions to take when concerns regarding a resident's capacity to self-administer are identified.

Emergency procedures such as the employees to be notified, the local poison information center telephone number, the person responsible for decision making, and the physician, clinic, emergency room, or comparable medical personnel to be contacted in the event of a medication emergency;
Procedures regarding management of medications including disposal of discontinued or out-of-date medications;
Definitions and procedures for documenting and reporting medication errors;
Procedures to flag allergies and other critical information; and
Requirements for staff training.
Each admission agreement shall include a written procedure for handling discharge and transfer of the resident that complies with these rules.

All Community Living Arrangements must maintain a monthly plan for specific staff coverage in advance of the month, a record of actual staff coverage, and a plan for provision of all required services.

There shall be established procedures and mechanisms for alerting and caring for residents in case of emergencies and for evacuating them to safety. An evacuation plan with clear instructions shall be available within each residence.
The Community Living Arrangement shall have and enforce effective procedures to minimize to the greatest extent possible the use of restraints.

sections: Code of conduct, including prohibited acts, employee reporting process, annual signed acknowledgment and discipline (.05(8)(a))
Abuse, neglect, exploitation and incident reporting (.05(8)(f))
Medical support devices and restrictive interventions (.05(8)(g))
Admissions and discharges, refunds, transfer of records and belongings, and cooperative living (.05(8)(h))
Staffing, staff training and credential verification (.05(8)(j))

official.notes: No single policy checklist or review form exists for this program. The DBHDD CLA Application Packet (v. 1/1/2026) lists only application paperwork and contains no policy checklist. Policy content therefore comes from the regulation sections that list required written policies. (1) Rule 290-9-37-.07(1), (3) and (6) is the current codified rule, and the 2026 application packet still points applicants to it. (2) Proposed Rule 82-13-1-.05(8) expands that list. Its public notice describes it as the list of required governing-body policies and says the new chapter will amend 290-9-37. I could not verify adoption, so confirm the status on DBHDD's 'Privacy, Rules & Regulations' page before finalizing. The proposed text contains drafting glitches: two items are labeled '(n)', and some cross-references are off. The items are reproduced as drafted. Section references inside the proposed rule point to .12 (admission), .14 (medications), .15 (rights), .16 (medical support devices) and .17 (restraints), so those sections should be cross-referenced in the manual. Suggested organization: one manual with a table of contents and policies in the same order as .05(8)(a) through (o). Number each policy with the rule item it satisfies. Add a crosswalk to 290-9-37-.07(3)(a)-(l) and (6)(a)-(e) so a reviewer can find each item under either rule. Keep the emergency/disaster plan as its own section covering all required scenarios, including the 30-minute elopement reporting. The packet gives no policy-upload slot, but the rules require the policies to exist before a license is issued, and surveys (announced or unannounced) can require production of records. Surveys by DBHDD are described in proposed rule .07. After a survey report, a written corrective action plan is due within 15 days, and a dispute may be offered within 10 days. Submit the application online through the GAHLES portal (https://gahles.dch.georgia.gov/). Initial review takes 30 business days. Send questions to Licensure.Application@dbhdd.ga.gov. A separate license is required for each residence. Proposed capacity is no more than four residents. Because these sites deliver CRA services under DBHDD contracts and the NOW/COMP waivers, also check the DBHDD DD provider manuals and DBHDD policies for additional requirements. I did not extract those manuals' policy requirements. Personnel-file items, the training and background-check requirements (.08), and the admission agreement contents (.12(7)) are operational or record requirements in the proposed rule, not listed policy items. Address them in the staffing and admission policies.
